cim: Eugene library holds workshop to educate public on how to opt out of artificial intelligence - Lookout Eugene-Springfield
cim_eredeti: Eugene library holds workshop to educate public on how to opt out of artificial intelligence - Lookout Eugene-Springfield
szoveg_eredeti:
The event, created and designed by the library, was based on giving people agency in how they use AI. For many, the use of AI, induces fear, curiosity and anger.

Elly Hutchinson, a library assistant, came up with the idea and designed the packets that accompanied the workshop. She said patrons had been asking a lot of questions about Google’s AI Overviews, the summaries that now appear at the top of search results.

Hutchinson said the openness of the format was intentional, citing that various folks might have different needs regarding AI on their devices. Hutchinson hopes to hold the workshop again. LIMITED TIME

If attendees ran into speed bumps along the way, four library staff and volunteers were there to help them.

“I feel overwhelmed by all the information,” Anna said. “I’ll look up one thing and suddenly my phone is inundated with this crap.”

“This event was more of an AI baseline on how to turn it off,” Sutherland said. “And drop-in tech help is just a little broader.” LIMITED TIME

Leo Heffron is a 2026 intern with the Charles Snowden Program for Excellence in Journalism.
